GOAL/G6: THE DESK PORTION OF andy/FACE.md, IN LINE WITH goal/G5

ANDY, VERBATIM
- 2026-10-05: "prime goal with desk-portion of FACE.md"
- 2026-10-05: "adapt box to be in line with G5 changes"
- To Q1 (ruleDetails shows older versions?): "No. the agents know it, and can bring it up, if neccessary."
- To Q2 (the header-area element: part of G6 or its own item?): "core. grant will be issued."

The source is andy/FACE.md, section "spirit/run/shell/desk/desk.js"; below it is read with his goal/G5 rulings, which win where they differ. The server side is built (goal/G5.5, G5.6, G5.7); this goal is the face.

GENERAL (FACE.md)
- All my chat-log entries left-aligned, not right-aligned.
- Chat log entries for everybody in bubbles, separated vertically by 1em.
- The header area, as in desk and deskDetails, a shell element every app can use: core, his grant to be issued on the files it touches.

A NEW TAB, "Rules", BETWEEN "Team" AND "Musings"
- The data is the desk server's rules table (goal/G5.5): key rule/N, label (the label rule, 64 bytes), type ui | code | design | desk, status proposed | active | deleted, text a paragraph of up to 2048 bytes with line breaks kept (G5.5: "2048 for now.", in place of FACE.md's one Kilobyte).
- 1. The new bubble: type, label and text, then a new button: rule.add, the rule comes in proposed. Agents may add one too (G5.5: "why not?").
- 2. The search bubble: a search box and 7 toggles (4 types, 3 statuses): rules.search {text, types, statuses}, the newest version of each rule, answering key, label, type, status.
- 3. The list, a row per rule: status (proposed ICON.EDIT, active ICON.LOCK, deleted ICON.DEAD), label, type, key. A row opens ruleDetails.

THE ruleDetails DIALOG (a new dialog app beside deskDetails)
- The header area, its top edge held under the shell's titlebar while the dialog scrolls: title key and label; buttons:
  - the version button, his alone: rule.version {key, text, status} makes the draft one new version (G5.5: "i prefer to negotiate, and create an updated version with one button/verb that belongs to me.");
  - activate (armable) and delete, each one quick version with that status (G5.5 Q6).
- The textbox of the rule, edited by him; what he types is saved as his draft (rule.draft, on the server, read back by rule.get; it writes no history), until the version button (G5.5 Q7).
- No older versions in the dialog: the agents know rule.history and bring a version up when needed.
- The chat area, styled like deskDetails': chat.add and item.chat under rule/N; no cap or split triggers. "in this chat, the agents may propose alterations to parts of the rule, or advocate for status changes for this rule."

THE "Musings" TAB (FACE.md; G5.5: "is pure ui")
- Each musing in its own bubble, maybe with the header area's background colour.
- 1em between the input textarea and each bubble.

WHAT THE FACE NEEDS TO KNOW BESIDES
- Every rule change is pushed: rules.md in the repo, and a desk line in the group chat (goal/G5.8).
- A goal now offers Close (goal/G5.6); the "are you sure?" while its items are open is the face's.

Waiting: his Go (no open question).
- His Go per item.

items.title: the header-area shell element (core): sticky under the titlebar, for desk, deskDetails and ruleDetails
items.box:
THE HEADER-AREA SHELL ELEMENT

WHAT IT IS
- One shell element, the header area: an empty div an app fills, held under the shell's titlebar while the app scrolls, opaque and above the content. Nothing else: what goes inside stays each app's.

SHAPE
- spirit/run/shell/js/appHeader/appHeader.js, one file per element as iconSelector.js is: it adds createAppHeader() to window.spiritElements, which the shell hands to apps as api.ui.elements.
- createAppHeader() returns the div: position sticky, its top the titlebar's measured height, measured in one place and again when the window resizes, the header background, a z-index above the content.
- index.html loads it beside iconSelector.js (index.html 1425).
- desk (desk.js 829-836, 958) and deskDetails (deskDetails.js 74, 95) move onto it, and their two copies of that div and its measuring are removed.
- ruleDetails (goal/G6.4) uses it from the start.

CORE AND GRANT (after goal/G6.7)
- Under the core rule G6.7 lands (his answers there), spirit/run/shell/js/appHeader/appHeader.js and spirit/run/index.html are core; desk.js and deskDetails.js are apps, not core. One G check on this item names the two core files.
- Blocked by goal/G6.7, so the commit check reads the new rule when this is built.

ANDY, VERBATIM
- FACE.md: "shell app apps/dialog apps can have a header area. this header area behaves like the header area in both desk and deskDetails. we want a shell element that facilitates that."
- FACE.md, ruleDetails: "it's upper edge sticks to the the lower edge of the shell's titlebar, when the user scrolls down in the dialog"
- "split as proposed" / "core. grant will be issued." / "the shape only produces the div container for the app to fill in, and provides only the sticking functionality?" / "fill in the shape and" "cap" / "the OPEN item here is no longer relevant." / "huh, shouldn't it be: Grant: add spirit/run/shell/js/appHeader/appHeader.js (core) what you do in spirit/run/shell/deskDetails/deskDetails.js etc... needs no grant."

Blocks goal/G6.4.

- desk and deskDetails move onto it, so the two copies go (eradicate what it replaces).

- In plain words, today: core = everything under spirit/run/js/, plus any shell app whose manifest says intrinsic: true (now deskDetails and the other intrinsic apps); spirit/run/shell/js/ is not core.
What should core be: spirit/run/js/ and spirit/run/shell/js/ (the system), with no app core at all?

tell me, from a system design point of view, which way is correct?

and where the hell is coreFiles.js anyway?

wsl: it lives at spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js, beside commitCheck.js which reads it.
By design, core is what other code depends on, so one change can break many: the node (spirit/run/js/) and the shell's shared layer (spirit/run/shell/js/, and its frame: index.html, elements.css, tokens.css). An app, intrinsic or not, is a leaf: a change to it breaks only itself; "intrinsic" means shipped with the shell, not depended upon.
So your way is the correct one: system core, apps not.

Your way is the correct one: core is what every app stands on, and an app is never core.
- Core: spirit/run/js/ (the node, the kernel, the client shell.js) and spirit/run/shell/js/ (the elements the shell hands every app), and index.html, which loads them.
- Not core: every app in spirit/run/shell/<app>/, intrinsic or not; "intrinsic" says an app ships and starts by default, not that it is the system.
Where: spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js, inside the desk server's folder, read only by commitCheck.js beside it; the system's own definition of core sitting inside one app is odd too.
Fix in G6.1: core = spirit/run/js/, spirit/run/shell/js/, spirit/run/index.html; no app core?

ubi, from a system-design standpoint:

Core means code whose change can hit every app or every agent — it must not change without you seeing it. Non-core means code that affects only one app. Those two are the right lines.

Shell/js/ is shared UI building blocks (iconSelector, appHeader, dialogs). Change one, every app's UI shifts: core. Shell/<app>/ is one app's own code, change it and only that app changes: not core, whatever its deployment flag says.

'intrinsic: true' in a manifest is a deployment property (the app ships bundled with the node and loads automatically). It is orthogonal to change-safety. coreFiles.js today conflates the two, which is why deskDetails is treated as core (its manifest says intrinsic) while shell/js/ is treated as app code. That is backwards against the design idea; your reading is the system-design one.

The file lives at spirit/run/js/coreFiles.js.

So the correct rule: core = spirit/run/js/ + spirit/run/shell/js/, nothing per-app; deployment stays in the manifests but drops out of the core question. Fix fits in G6.1 or wants its own item.
wsl: agreed, plus the shell's two shared stylesheets, spirit/run/shell/elements.css and tokens.css: every app is drawn by them, so they belong with index.html.
One correction to ubi: the file is spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js (there is no spirit/run/js/coreFiles.js); the rest of ubi's reading matches wsl's and mine.
wsl, one correction to ubi's line: there is no spirit/run/js/coreFiles.js; the file is spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js, in the desk server's folder.
ubi, correcting the file path in my last line: coreFiles.js is at spirit/run/process/js/desk/coreFiles.js (beside commitCheck.js), as wsl noted — not spirit/run/js/. The design framing stands.

WHERE IT COMES FROM

DESK SERVER: A SUB-GOAL ONLY BY HIS SPLIT

ANDY, VERBATIM
- In goal/G5.4: "when i say split, that becomes implicit/obvious and the item should be marked as sub-goal"
- 2026-10-06, in goal/G6: "an item becomes a sub-goal only when i say split, the box of that item must then only contain references to it's blockers, and it can no longer be marked as a coding item."

- 2026-10-06: "while you're in DeskServer: can you also make sure that in design mode as well, OPEN is help in red-questions?" / "i want mechanical tracking of design-greens. Yes i want opens to light up my list with ERROR icons."

THE DIVERGENCE (found by claude-windows adding goal/G6.7)
- goal/G5.4 as built marks an item sub-goal whenever a session adds a new item blocking it (desk.js session.set; claude-ubuntu's red deskLimbo section 2 asserted that). Adding G6.7 in front of G6.1 to G6.6 would make all six sub-goals, though he never said split.

THE SHAPE (claude-windows; Andy: "accepted.")
- session.set takes split: [id] naming the item he split; only that item is marked sub-goal; a new blocking item alone marks nothing.
- A sub-goal is not a code item: the split clears its code mark, and a session cannot mark it code again.
- Its box holds only references to its blockers: the agent writing the split rewrites the box to that list; the desk does not police the text.
- deskLimbo's section 2 changes to the explicit split.

DESIGN-GREEN, TRACKED BY THE DESK
- An open point is a red question, never box text: a box.write with an OPEN section is refused.
- An item is design-green when it has no open red question; its facts say so (green), and an open question lights his ERROR in the List, as asks do today.
- His End design, and a Go, are refused while any item in that scope is not design-green.
- Gap for the face: the List draws no icon on a goal's own row (shell/desk/desk.js 589), so a question on a goal stays dark; that row needs the same ERROR.
